newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Cresson blocks negative beef aid report.
newsitem.headline: Cresson blocks negative beef aid report.

text.p: A French EU Commissioner has blocked a report by European Commission beef experts concluding that beef farmers did not need further compensation for losses due to mad cow disease, Commission sources said.
The report, which was due to have been approved without discussion on Friday, was stopped by the EU's French Commissioner Edith Cresson, a source said.
The EU approved in July 850 million Ecus of emergency aid for beef producers and member states were authorised to provide a further 850 million Ecus.
Income losses were estimated by Commission experts at between 1.0 and 1.2 billion Ecus.

Cresson's move came just before a meeting EU farm ministers next week to discuss a package of beef market support measures and production cuts following a drop in demand due to consumer concern over beef safety.
French cattle producers staged protests in central France on Friday demanding government aid to compensate for falling meat consumption due to fears of mad cow disease.
Farmers leaders say French meat sales have dropped by up to 25 percent. EU meat demand is down by an average 15 percent.
